communications.subject: Oregon Public Records Law Request: Talent Police Department Flock Camera policy, invoice, map, and contracts
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting a copy of the following records, that have already been requested to Talent Police Department. By requesting previously produced records, I am hopeful that this request will require minimal labor to locate, review and produce the records. Please let me know if you need any additional information or clarification regarding the records I am seeking.

The records I am seeking are:

(1) all policies Talent Police Department has that oversee and/or regulate the operation and use of Automated License Plate Readers, including the operation and use of Flock, Vigilant, Axon, or any similar ALPR programs and softwares
(2) a copy of any and all invoices Talent Police Department has between any and all Automated License Plate Readers softwares and programs, including Flock, Vigilant, Axon, or any similar ALPR programs and softwares
(3) a map of all ALPR cameras that Talent Police Department owns, operates or has access to
(4) a copy of any and all license and user agreements, contracts, memorandums of understanding or other similar type documents that describe and/or regulate the use, retention, collection, and sharing of ALPR data including but not limited to the agreements between Flock, Vigilant, Axon, or any similar ALPR programs and softwares

Please segregate all non-exempt material, and “black out” rather than “white out” any exempt material. Please cite specific exemptions in every instance that  the public body claims an exemption.

Thank you so much!

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Southern Oregon Flock Off

title: Drone as First Responder and Skydio dock program records

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Drone as First Responder and Skydio dock program records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

In January 2026, the Federal Way City Council approved a Drone as First Responder (DFR) program using Skydio Dock for X10 systems. I request the following existing records in the Department's possession, created or modified between January 1, 2025 and the date this request is processed:

1. Contracts, purchase orders, and agreements with Skydio, including costs;
2. Records identifying the locations or siting of drone docks;
3. DFR program policies, procedures, evaluation criteria, and success metrics;
4. Privacy impact assessments or civil-liberties reviews conducted for the program;
5. Flight or deployment logs for DFR missions flown since the program began, sufficient to determine the date, time, general location, and purpose of each deployment.

This request does not seek video or imagery recorded by the drones. I prefer electronic delivery. Please notify me in advance if any copying or production fees will exceed $50.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robin Monks

communications.subject: Confirmation - P-2026-3419 (Federal Way Police Department - Police Records)
communications.communication:
Dear Robin Monks, 
  
 The Federal Way Police Department - Police Records received your request and we look forward to assisting you with your records search. 
  
 Your assigned request number and security key are listed below. Please retain this information to track the progress of your request and to download records from the Records Portal. 
  
 Request Number: Request Number: P-2026-3419  
 Security Key: ABE4ED88 
  
 When will I receive a response to my request? 
  
 City Records and Police Records Requests 
  
 The City Clerk Department is responsible for managing requests for all general city records, except those maintained by the Federal Way Police Department or the Municipal Court. The Federal Way Police Department is responsible for coordinating, tracking, and fulfilling requests for police records. Court records are addressed separately below. 
  
 Pursuant to RCW 42.56.520, you will receive a response within five (5) business days of receipt of your City or Police records request, with one of the following: 
  
 Providing the record(s); 
 Providing a link to the records posted on the City’s website; 
 Providing a reasonable estimate of the time necessary to provide records; 
 Seeking clarification of the request; or 
 Denying the request 
  
 Additional time to respond may be required to locate and assemble records, notify affected third parties, or determine whether disclosure exemptions apply. The five-day response period begins on the next business day after receipt of the request (weekends and holidays excluded). 
  
 The Public Records Act (RCW 42.56) does not require a governmental agency to create new information/records, conduct legal research, or answer questions. For more information, please view the City of Federal Way Public Records Policy.  
  
 Municipal Court Records Requests 
  
 Court records are subject to release under the WA State Court General Rules, GR 31–Access to Court Records and GR 31.1–Access to Administrative Records. Court records are not subject to the Public Records Act.   
  
 Questions? 
  
 If you have any questions, contact information for each type of record request is listed below: 
  
 Police Records
Phone: 253-835-6700
Email: PD-PRA@federalwaywa.gov

Phone: 253-835-3000

 City Records

 Thank you for using the City of Federal Way Public Records Request Center. 
  
 Sincerely, 

Police Records

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

Please supply the full personnel files of the following individual:

Isaiah White, former CPS teacher and current school board candidate for subdistrict 6A.

This includes any resumes, applications, any job recommendations, promotions, professional license credentials and verification records. Please include a work/salary history. Please include any investigative materials - investigative memorandums, disciplinary actions (suspensions, leaves of absence that stem from disciplinary action), incident reports, EOCO investigations, Office of Civil Rights determinations, non-disciplinary memorandum of understandings, non-union misconduct form, full warning resolutions and any complaints or claims/lawsuits/settlements. Please include any safety plans. Please include any separation agreements and any other disclosure agreements.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Megan Sheahan

Chicago Public Schools (CPS) responds to all public records requests in accordance with the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 ILCS 140/1 et seq. 
Due to the volume and complexity of requests received in the normal course of business, CPS is extending the time for its initial response to your request by an additional 5 business days (to 10 business days total beginning on the first business day following receipt of the request) pursuant to 5 ILCS 140/3(e)(v) which allows for the examination and evaluation of the requested records by personnel to determine if they are exempt from disclosure under Section 7 of Illinois FOIA or should be revealed only with appropriate deletions.

Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2427102/ 
RESPONSE: Documents responsive to your request are available to download via the CPS FOIA Center at www.cps.edu/FOIARequests . Please log in with your username and password to access the records. Please note that certain private information (personal descriptions, employee ID numbers, college transcripts, social security numbers, citizenship status, signatures, personal addresses/phone numbers, medical information, etc.) was redacted pursuant to 5 ILCS 140/7. Specifically, section 7(1)(b) which exempts certain private information as defined by section 2(c-5) and section 7(1)(c) which exempts personal information contained within public records, the disclosure of which would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy, unless the disclosure is consented to in writing by the individual subject of the information. “Unwarranted invasion of personal privacy” means the disclosure of information that is highly personal or objectionable to a reasonable person and in which the subject’s right to privacy outweighs any legitimate public interest in obtaining the information. 5 ILCS 140/7(1)(a) exempts “ information specifically prohibited from disclosure by federal or State Law … ” (5 ILCS 140/7(1)(a)) Specifically, 105 ILCS 5/10-21.9 (b) states that “ any information concerning the record of convictions obtained by the president of the school board or the regional superintendent shall be confidential and may only be transmitted to the superintendent of the school district or his designee, the appropriate regional superintendent if the check was requested by the school district, the presidents of the appropriate school boards if the check was requested from the Department of State Police by the regional superintendent, the State Superintendent of Education, the State Teacher Certification Board, any other person necessary to the decision of hiring the applicant for employment, or for clarification purposes the Department of State Police or Statewide Sex Offender Database, or both.” 
You have a right to have the denial of your request reviewed by the Public Access Counselor (PAC) at the Office of the Illinois Attorney General. 5 ILCS 140/9.5(a). You can file your Request for Review with the PAC by writing to: Leah Bartelt; Public Access Counselor Office of the Attorney General 500 South 2nd Street Springfield, Illinois 62706 E-mail: public.access@ilag.gov 877-299-3642 You also have the right to seek judicial review of your denial by filing a lawsuit in the State circuit court. 5 ILCS 140/11. If you choose to file a Request for Review with the PAC, you must do so within 60 calendar days of the date of this denial letter. 5 ILCS 140/9.5(a). Please note that you must include a copy of your original FOIA request and this denial letter when filing a Request for Review with the PAC. Sincerely, Marisol Muneton Freedom of Information Act Officer Chicago Public Schools

communications.subject: Government Records Access and Management Act Request: West Valley City Flock
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Government Records Access and Management Act, I hereby request the following records:

Related to automated license plate reader (ALPR) or "Flock Safety" camera systems operated by or in partnership with the West Valley Police and West Valley:

All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, or other instruments between West Valley Police and Flock Safety, Inc., or any related entity, including any amendments or renewals. (No date restriction.)

All invoices, payment records, and purchase orders related to Flock Safety equipment, software, or services. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All data retention policies governing footage, license plate reads, or associated metadata collected by Flock cameras. (No date restriction.)

All written policies, procedures, or general orders governing officer access to, and use of, Flock camera data. (No date restriction.)

All records reflecting the total number of Flock cameras deployed, their locations, and dates of installation. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All records of third-party data sharing, including but not limited to agreements or logs of data shared with other law enforcement agencies, federal agencies, or private parties. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All audit logs, access logs, or query logs reflecting searches of Flock camera data by West Valley Police employees or contractors. (January 1, 2024 through present.)

All records reflecting complaints, grievances, or legal challenges related to the Flock camera program. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All communications, including email and internal messaging platform records, between West Valley Police employees and Flock Safety, Inc. representatives regarding the procurement, deployment, expansion, or renewal of the program. (January 1, 2024 through present.)

Any privacy impact assessments, legal reviews, or internal memoranda regarding the program's compliance with Texas law. (No date restriction.)

If any portion of a responsive record is withheld, please identify each withheld document by description, date, author, and recipient in a detailed withholding log, and specify the statutory exception claimed for each.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emma E Metos

communications.communication:
Dear Requester.

Thank you for your reply. This correspondence confirms the receipt of your FOIA request, seeking all quarterly reports, summaries, or updates transmitted by the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA) to the FTC concerning Funeral Rule Offenders Program (FROP) participants and/or missed deadlines, including any cover emails and attachments within the date range for record search from January 1, 2018 to February 19, 2026.

Due to the significant backlog caused by the federal shutdown, the FTC is processing requests as quickly as possible but has not yet begun to process yours. As soon as we are able, an individual FTC employee will reach out to let you know that they are starting work on your request and will provide their contact information.

In the meantime, if you have questions or concerns, please reach out to us at foia@ftc.gov<mailto:foia@ftc.gov>. You may also check the status of your FOIA request by visiting http://www.ftc.gov/about-ftc/foia/foia-reading-rooms/track-your-foia-request. This report is updated at the end of each month. If you should have any questions regarding your request, please contact us at foia@ftc.gov<mailto:foia@ftc.gov>. In any call or future correspondence concerning the request, please refer to the following case number FOIA-2026-00484.

title: WA ALPR: A: External Access Audit Logs (1/4) (Walla Walla Police Department)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: WA ALPR: A: External Access Audit Logs (1/4) (Walla Walla Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All system audit logs, as natively maintained in your agency's systems or your vendor's systems, reflecting access to your agency's ALPR system or any system used to store, process, or query ALPR data (e.g., Axon Evidence.com, Flock Safety portal, Motorola/Vigilant), by users affiliated with any agency other than your agency.

2. All system audit logs, as natively maintained, reflecting the Originating Agency Identifier (ORI) or agency name associated with each external query of your agency's ALPR system.

3. All system audit logs, as natively maintained, reflecting the user identifier, badge number, or account name associated with each query of your agency's ALPR system, whether the querying user was internal or external to your agency.

4. All records identifying which external agencies are currently authorized to access, query, or receive data from your agency's ALPR system, including any configuration record, permissions list, access control list, or authorized-agency registry maintained in your ALPR platform.  If this information exists only as a display within a software interface, a screenshot, faithful reproduction, or export of that display to any available file format is an acceptable and required form of production.

Note on vendor-held records: In Rodriguez v. City of Stanwood & Sedro-Woolley (Skagit County Superior Court, Nov. 6, 2025), the court held that ALPR data held by a third-party SaaS vendor on behalf of a government agency is a public record subject to PRA disclosure. Vendor custody does not relieve your agency of its production obligation. Each request below that encompasses vendor-held records is made on this basis. Please retrieve and produce all responsive records held by your ALPR vendor(s) on your agency's behalf.

Note on record creation: I am seeking existing records only. I understand that no agency is required to create a new record in response to a PRA request. However, producing a screenshot or other faithful reproduction of an existing electronic display is not creating a new record — it is reproducing an existing one, in the same manner as photocopying or scanning a paper document. Agencies cannot evade their production obligation by characterizing screenshots of existing system displays as "new records."

I am requesting these records for research and public interest purposes, submitted through MuckRock, a nonprofit journalism platform. I request that your agency consider waiving any fees given that this request is submitted for research and public interest purposes and that electronic production of the requested records should entail minimal or no actual cost under RCW 42.56.120. For any anticipated costs, please notify me before incurring them so that I may prioritize or narrow the request. This notification requirement should not be construed as authorization to delay production of records for which no fee will be incurred pending resolution of fees for other records in this request

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Phil Mocek

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: 2026 Code violations
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

copies of public records concerning municipal code-enforcement actions within the City of Norman.

Specifically, I request a digital copy, spreadsheet, or log of all residential code-enforcement violations, citations, and notices issued from January 1, 2026, through the date this request is processed.

To limit clerical search time, please provide the information in its existing electronic format, such as Excel, CSV, or a text file. I am requesting only the following fields:

- Property owner’s or responsible party’s name
- Street address
- Violation type
- Date the violation was recorded or notice was issued

If the City does not maintain a centralized spreadsheet or log containing these fields, please provide the existing underlying electronic records from which this information can be extracted.

If any responsive record does not contain the property owner’s or responsible party’s name, please provide the remaining requested fields rather than withholding the entire record.

If the estimated cost will exceed $25, please provide an itemized estimate before processing the request. I request that any fees be waived because the records will be made available to the general public and concern the enforcement of municipal health, safety, and property-maintenance laws.

If any portion of this request is denied, withheld, or redacted, please identify the specific statutory exemption under the Oklahoma Open Records Act supporting that decision and release all reasonably segregable portions of the records.

Thank you for your attention and cooperation.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: 2026 Structure Fires
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I request public records concerning residential structure fires within the City of Norman.

Specifically, I request a digital spreadsheet, report, or incident log identifying all residential properties where the Norman Fire Department responded to a structure fire from January 1, 2026, through the date this request is processed.

To limit clerical search time, please provide the information in its existing electronic format, such as Excel, CSV, or a text file. Please include the following available fields:

- Property owner’s or responsible party’s name
- Property address
- Date of the fire
- Incident type
- Description or estimated extent of property damage

I am requesting a summary list or incident log rather than complete individual incident reports, photographs, medical information, 911 recordings, or investigative files.

If the Fire Department does not maintain the property owner’s name or any other field requested please provide the remaining requested fields available. If no centralized spreadsheet or log exists, please provide the existing underlying electronic records from which this information can be extracted.

If the estimated cost will exceed $25, please provide an itemized estimate before processing the request.

If any portion of this request is denied, withheld, or redacted, please identify the specific statutory exemption under the Oklahoma Open Records Act and release all reasonably segregable portions of the record

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Donald Davis (Msd Decatur Township)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Indiana Access to Public Records Act § 5-14-3-1 et seq., Mirror Indy is requesting the following Records related to the following current or former employees:

Donald Davis (6155-7950)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

communications.communication:
Dear Ms. Hopkins,



This correspondence is intended to follow-up with you on your public
records request seeking records related to Donald Davis.  Each of your
requests will be addressed in turn:



*Your request*:  Hiring date



*Response: * The Employee Status record showing Mr. Davis' hire date is
available for a cost of $0.10.



*Your request: * Termination date



*Response: * The Employee Status record showing Mr. Davis’ separation date
is available for a cost of $0.10.



*Your request:*  Compensation



*Response*:  An Employee Status record showing Mr. Davis’ compensation and
a compensation record showing his final unused vacation days payout and
final work days payout are available for a cost of $0.10 (1 of these
records is included in those listed above)



*Your request:*  Commendations



*Response:*  No records exist in the files of the School District that are
responsive to this request.



*Your request:*  Assignments/job roles



*Response:*  The Employee Status record showing Mr. Davis’ position held
with the School District is available (included in a record listed above).



*Your request*:  Disciplinary actions and the factual basis for
disciplinary actions



*Response: * The Indiana Access to Public Records Act only requires the
release of the factual basis for a disciplinary action in which final
action has been taken and that resulted in the employee being suspended,
demoted, or discharged.  See IC 5-14-3-4(b)(8).  All other disciplinary
records are permitted to be exempted from disclosure pursuant to IC
5-14-3-4(b)(8).  No disciplinary records exist that are subject to
mandatory disclosure under Indiana law.  To the extent you are requesting
disciplinary records beyond the scope of the records that are required to
be produced, your request is denied pursuant to IC 5-14-3-4(b)(8).  The
individual authorizing this denial is the Superintendent of the
Metropolitan School District of Decatur Township, Dr. Scott Collins.



*Your request:*  Letters of resignation



*Response: * The resignation notice is available for a cost of $0.10.

The MSD of Decatur Township accepts cash/coin payments in person at 5275
Kentucky Ave. Indianapolis, IN 46221 during regular business hours of 8:00

accepted.

Public Records Officer

NMSA 1978, §§ 14-2-1(A) and 14-2-6; State ex rel. Newsome v. Alarid, 1977-NMSC-076, ¶ 11, 90 N.M. 790, 794; NMSA 1978, § 14-2-1(H); 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(a)(1) and 164.512(e)(1). NMSA 1978, § 31-21-6.  These records are also protected by a policy adopted by the Secretary of the Corrections Department.  NMSA 1978, §§ 9-3-5(E) and 33-1-6(B) (authority to adopt rules for Department operation); CD-040101(C)(1)(g)(2)-(3).  The records are therefore exempt from public inspection and are being withheld.  NMSA 1978, § 14-2-1(H). TO:   Ryann Sargent, DDOT FOIA Officer <ryann.sargent@dc.gov>; Victoria Fleming, DC WATER FOIA Officer <victoria.fleming@dc.gov>CC: oig.hotline@epa.gov; richard.jackson2@dc.gov; sharon.kershbaum@dc.gov; david.gadis@dcwater.com; foia@dcwater.com; ddot.foia@dc.gov; pmendelson@dccouncil.us; callen@dccouncil.gov; serena_bellew@nps.gov; michael_donato@nps.gov; dondrae.maiden@sol.doi.gov; Square5815Oversight@gmail.com  SUBJECT: EXPEDITED FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT (FOIA) REQUEST: Work Orders, TOPS Permits, and Dispatch Records for Square 5815 / Morris Rd SE

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act, D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq., I hereby request expedited production of the following public records:

1. WORK ORDERS & ASSET MANAGEMENT: All internal DC Water work orders, service tickets, maintenance requests, and work tickets generated within DC Water’s enterprise asset management system (e.g., Maximo) from September 1, 2026, through October 4, 2026, concerning Square 5815, Lot 802, 16th St SE, or the adjacent public right-of-way.
2. PUBLIC SPACE PERMITS & TOPS LOGS: The complete DDOT Transportation Online Permitting System (TOPS) permit application, permit approval file, fee calculation, and approved signage documentation associated with:
   - Reason: "Sewer Emergency Repair"
   - Date Printed: 09/02/2026
   - Contact Agency: DCWATER/ OPS
   - Contact Telephone Number: (202) 612-3400
   - Location: Sixteenth St SE / Square 5815
3. DISPATCH & CONTRACTOR LOGS:  All contractor invoices, subcontractor task orders, equipment mobilization manifests (specifically including Titan vacuum trucks and mechanical bypass pumps), and employee overtime/timesheet records for work performed at this site on October 2, October 3, and October 4, 2026.
4. SIGN MODIFICATION & PERMIT EXTENSION RECORDS:  All communications, emails, work orders, or instructions authorizing or referencing the manual date alteration ("10-9") or extension of the emergency no parking placard printed on 09/02/2026.
5. NATIVE FORMAT & METADATA PRESERVATION DEMAND: Produce all electronic records, including enterprise database logs (Maximo/TOPS) and internal emails, in their native digital formats with all rich metadata intact (including creation dates, modification dates, author IDs, routing data, and system audit trails). Do not "flatten," export, or print digital database records to PDF if such conversion strips, degrades, or destroys the underlying forensic metadata.

Expedited processing is requested pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(f) because there is an urgency to inform the public concerning actual government activity involving an active structural landslide and an uncontained public health biohazard adjacent to a designated public school pedestrian route.

Matt Chapman
Free Our Info, NFP

communications.communication:
Here's the documentation. This was given to another department in another state, so pardon any differences in context:

Steps for exporting email metadata from Office 365:
0. Username must have access to search and export eDiscovery reports. If not, your IT department should have access to either grant the required permissions, or run through these steps themselves.
1. From Internet Explorer, log into https://protection.office.com/. 
2. Navigate to "Search & Investigation" -> "eDiscovery" and create a new case.
3. Open the case, then create a new search through "Search" -> "New search"
4. Add a "Type" condition and select, "E-mail messages".
5. Under "Locations" -> "Specific locations" -> "Modify...".
6. Toggle the location that includes "Exchange email" and click "Save".
7. Click "Save & run" and give the search a name.
8. Navigate to "More" -> "Export results", then select the following options:
-Output options: "All items, excluding [...]"
-Export Exchange content as: "Individual messages"
9. Navigate to Export -> "[Name of export]_Export".
10. Click "Download results" and launch the "Unified Export Tool".
11. Paste the export page's "Export key" into the tool's key field.
12. Choose a save location and click "Start"
13. Open "results.csv" from the saved location.
14. Delete all columns that are not the requested metadata and save.

(Please note that depending on the size of the csv files, this may need to be done in batches through the use of a date or sender/receiver conditional within the search query. Similar can be said about filtering down to just your office's department's email addresses.)

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: 2026 code violations
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I request copies of public records concerning municipal code-enforcement actions within the City of Edmond.

Specifically, I request a digital copy, spreadsheet, or log of all residential code-enforcement violations, citations, and notices issued from January 1, 2026, through the date this request is processed.

To limit clerical search time, please provide the information in its existing electronic format, such as Excel, CSV, or a text file. I am requesting only the following fields:

- Property owner’s or responsible party’s name
- Street address
- Violation type
- Date the violation was recorded or notice was issued

If the City does not maintain a centralized spreadsheet or log containing these fields, please provide the existing underlying electronic records from which this information can be extracted.

If any responsive record does not contain the property owner’s or responsible party’s name, please provide the remaining requested fields rather than withholding the entire record.

If the estimated cost will exceed $25, please provide an itemized estimate before processing the request. I request that any fees be waived because the records will be made available to the general public and concern the enforcement of municipal health, safety, and property-maintenance laws.

If any portion of this request is denied, withheld, or redacted, please identify the specific statutory exemption under the Oklahoma Open Records Act supporting that decision and release all reasonably segregable portions of the records.

Thank you for your attention and cooperation.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: ICE Death Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

ICE detainee death records for Julio Cesar Chirino Peralta, a 32 year-old migrant from Nicaragua, who died following his detention at the Port Isabel Detention Center on October 8, 2023 (see https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddrJulioCesarChirinoPeralta.pdf): 

1. The Office of Professional Responsibility Detainee Death Review (search the External Reviews and Analysis Unit within ICE OPR); 
2. The Creative Corrections Healthcare and Security Compliance Analysis report (search ERAU); 
3. the IHSC Mortality Review (search the ICE Health Service Corps); 
4. The IHSC Root Cause Analysis, if any (search IHSC). 

We request expedited processing of this request pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e) and provide the following statements in support of our request under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 USC 1746: 

1. At the time of this request, ICE deaths in custody have doubled the highest levels from previous years of the Biden administration. https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/number-deaths-ice-custody-already-double-last-year-rcna154659#:~:text=NBC%20News%20Tipline-,The%20number%20of%20deaths%20in%20ICE%20custody%20is%20already%20more,of%20the%20six%20preceding%20years.
2. The current rate of in-custody ICE deaths is on track to exceed any non-COVID year since FY17. See: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11007418/; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7870381/
3. Deaths in ICE custody have been the subject of widespread, ongoing media coverage and extensive policy advocacy and discussion. See, e.g. ,https://www.npr.org/2023/11/08/1211316303/ice-releases-investigation-into-immigrants-death-after-months-of-inexcusable-del; https://www.yahoo.com/news/number-deaths-ice-custody-already-133000592.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAALCThkPLfU2ufNLo_I3yqmeUO38qEyUSI4U597M71FTc3npyfor0xVw-REfCt-2anUv5517ufGPQZZuU4KKiJ98axkk_ivGQf5e9Gu_gYZaHzjunplOd3-7tEQTfDoPBn6g0zjNvYt8aKSYJBBN9iLv2gvnes6k94yMIMemD-0yw; https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/30/us/migrant-death-ice-custody-recommended-release/index.html.
4. There exist serious questions regarding the government's capacity to ensure safe and humane detention conditions that prevent deaths in ICE custody, based on available FOIA records obtained through federal litigation.  See, e.g., https://prismreports.org/2023/04/20/ice-gourgan-mirimanian-death-2018/; https://today.usc.edu/ice-deaths-custody-detention-medical-standards-violated-usc-study/
5. ICE has announced its intention to expand its detention system, potentially increasing the numbers of in-custody death to even higher levels. https://www.ice.gov/news/releases/ice-announces-ongoing-work-optimize-enforcement-resources
6. ICE has previously failed to accurately inform the public of its own internal agency conclusions about the events leading up to in-custody deaths. See, e.g., https://www.aclu.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/April-2024-ACLU-Letter-to-ICE-on-Torrance-Detention-Facility.pdf

There is a compelling need to obtain these records as soon as possible so that the public can understand the consequences of ICE's current detention management processes as the agency seeks to expand the system beyond its appropriated limit of 41,500 beds.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your 6/16/2024, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), for records pertaining to the death of Julio Cesar Chirino Peralta.  Your request was received in this office on 6/16/2024. 

Some information has already been made public at chrome-extension://efaidnbmnnnibpcajpcglclefindmkaj/https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddrJulioCesarChirinoPeralta.pdf and at https://www.ice.gov/news/releases/nicaraguan-national-ice-custody-dies. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

Provisions of the FOIA allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request.  We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS Interim FOIA regulations, as they apply to media requesters.  As a media requester, you will be charged 10 cents per page for duplication; the first 100 pages are free.  We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued. 

We have queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions, please contact FOIA Public Liaison, Daniel Edgington at 500 12th Street, SW, Washington DC 20536 or (866) 633-1182. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974. communications.subject: North Dakota Open Records Law Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Dakota Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Public Records Request — Minnesota Generative AI Records
communications.communication:
Subject: Public Records Request — AI Chatbot Interaction Logs

April 9, 2026

Data Practices Compliance Official
Minnesota IT Services (MNIT)
658 Cedar Street
St. Paul, MN 55155

Dear Data Practices Compliance Official,

I am writing on behalf of a team of researchers and journalists from Stanford University, the University of Southern California, KNKX Public Radio and the New York Times. We are studying how government agencies are adopting and using AI tools in their daily work.

We are writing to request records related to Minnesota's use of generative AI tools by state employees, including Microsoft Copilot Chat and the nebulaONE chatbot platform.

We are requesting the following records under Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3:

1. All interaction logs from Microsoft 365 Government Copilot Chat, nebulaONE, ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, or any other generative AI chatbot tool — including prompts submitted by state employees and responses generated by the AI — for the period from April 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed. We request these records in their native electronic format where available (e.g., HTML exports, JSON, or CSV).

2. Any policies, guidelines, acceptable use policies, or training materials governing state employee use of Microsoft Copilot Chat, nebulaONE, or other generative AI chatbot tools.

3. Any data retention or deletion policies applicable to AI chatbot interaction logs, including any schedules for automatic deletion of interaction data.

4. Administrative usage statistics for Microsoft Copilot Chat and nebulaONE showing number of users, sessions, and queries processed.

We are seeking the substantive content of AI interactions for research purposes. We do not need personally identifying information of individual employees (such as names and email addresses).

Minnesota was one of the first states to roll out Microsoft 365 Government Copilot Chat to executive branch employees at no cost as part of its existing Microsoft contract, beginning April 8, 2025 (see GovTech, "Minnesota Taps Free GenAI Through Microsoft Partnership," https://www.govtech.com/biz/minnesota-taps-free-genai-through-microsoft-partnership). All prompts, responses, and content remain within the Microsoft Government Community Cloud (GCC) environment. Additionally, MNIT is advancing the nebulaONE chatbot development tool with support from the Technology Modernization Fund and Microsoft investment funds to enable safe deployment of AI-powered services including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and custom chatbots (see MNIT, "Empowering State Employees with Secure, AI-Driven Tools," https://mn.gov/mnit/about-mnit/tmf/state-employee-ai-chat-bot-tools.jsp).

We note that records of this type have been made available in response to public records requests in other jurisdictions. See Cascade PBS, "WA City Officials Are Using ChatGPT to Write Government Documents" (Aug. 2025), https://www.cascadepbs.org/news/2025/08/wa-city-officials-are-using-chatgpt-to-write-government-documents/; see also Texas State AI Usage — Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT), MuckRock, https://www.muckrock.com/foi/texas-109/texas-state-ai-usage-texas-department-of-transportation-txdot-196227/#files.

The results of this research will be published in peer-reviewed academic venues and will contribute to public understanding of how public servants interact with AI systems. This request is made by an academic research institution for scholarly, non-commercial purposes; as such, we request a fee waiver or reduction. If a fee waiver is not granted, please inform me of estimated costs before proceeding. I am willing to pay fees up to $20.

I understand that this may be a novel type of records request and I am happy to answer any technical questions. Please feel free to contact me at the email address below.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Sincerely,
Alexander Spangher
Postdoctoral Researcher
Stanford University
alexspan@stanford.edu

P.S. To facilitate your response, we note that ChatGPT conversation histories can be exported by individual users via Settings > Data Controls > Export Data. For Microsoft Copilot, interaction histories may be available through the Microsoft 365 admin console or the Purview compliance center. For Google Gemini, interaction data may be available through Google Vault or Google Takeout. We are happy to provide additional technical guidance if that would be helpful.

P.P.S. The Minnesota Government Data Practices Act covers all "government data," defined as all data collected, created, received, maintained, or disseminated by a government entity regardless of physical form. Minn. Stat. § 13.02, subd. 7. Governor Walz's Executive Order 24-03 (2024) directed state agencies to develop policies for responsible AI use, including transparency and accountability provisions. Minnesota IT Services (MNIT) has issued guidance requiring that AI-generated content used in official business be treated as government data subject to existing retention schedules. Consistent with this trend nationally, NARA has made clear that chats and other electronic messages used for agency business are likely government records. NARA Bulletin 2023-02 (Jan. 5, 2023), https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/bulletins/2023/2023-02.

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Flock audit - large search access August 2026
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the following ID's of Flock Search records from Renton PD, I would like to get information on: 

- Number of results returned to the officer for this search.
- Count of the number of images that were accessed by the officer for this search.
- Number of images which were accessed from Renton's 24 camera Flock network, versus external to Renton's network.
- Description of images accessed by the officer (license plate, car make, model, camera location, etc)

For reference, this is the Renton PD ALPR page which implies there is a method to determine a number of images accessed for searches ( https://www.rentonwa.gov/Government/Departments-and-Offices/Police/Police-Transparency/Automated-License-Plate-Readers  Section: Searches )

Flock Search ID:
09650265-6932-4a98-95a1-55d3d1bc6b29

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brian Hughes

communications.subject: (U) USSOCOM 2026-087, 2026-144, 2026-145, 2026-289 and 2026-392 - Acknowledgements
communications.communication:
Classification: UNCLASSIFIED

Message Body Classification: UNCLASSIFIED

Dear Ms. Best,

This is in response to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request (copy attached) you submitted to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and it was subsequently referred to U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM).  It was assigned USSOCOM FOIA 2026-392.  In addition, the FBI previously referred documents to USSOCOM to review pertaining to this request, and they were assigned as USSOCOM FOIA control numbers 2026-087, 2026-144, 2026-145, and 2026-289.  We apologize that you did not receive acknowledgements from us previously for these other case numbers.  Please refer to these numbers should you have any questions concerning your request.

Your requests are being processed in accordance with procedural requirements promulgated in Department of Defense (DoD) Manual 5400.07, which is available on the internet at: https://open.defense.gov/Portals/23/Documents/FOIA/FOIA_Resources/DoDM%205400.07.pdf?ver=2017-03-15-135646-847.  The actual processing time will depend upon its complexity, whether it involves sensitive records, voluminous records, extensive searches, consultation among DoD components or other agencies, and our administrative workload.

We have placed you in the "News Media" category for fee purposes, which means you are obligated to pay for any duplication costs after the first 100 pages; however, depending on the size of the documents, we may provide the final releases on CD or electronically and no charges would be applicable.

The USSOCOM FOIA Office has a substantial number of pending FOIA cases; therefore, we process requests in a multi-track processing system based on the date of receipt and the amount of work and time involved in processing each request.  We estimate the time for completion to be approximately 4-6 months; it could be more or less.  If you wish to discuss this or have any other questions or concerns, please contact this office at FOIA@socom.mil<mailto:FOIA@socom.mil>.
Regards,
USSOCOM FOIA Team

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Pacific Coast Intermodal Port (PCIP) Port Infrastructure Development Program (PIDP) FY 2026 Grant Application
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

As it relates to the Port Infrastructure Development Program (PIDP), FY2026 round "Pacific Coast Intermodal Port (PCIP) Terminal Connection Project," Coos Bay, Oregon (awarded $11,250,000):**

a. The complete grant application as submitted, including all attachments, exhibits, and appendices
b. The advance grant notice
c. The executed Grant Agreement, including any amendments
d. The scoring and review records for the FY2026 PIDP round as they pertain to this application: the scoring rubric/criteria, individual reviewer score sheets and written comments, the applicant ranking table, and any interagency or technical review memoranda.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Wyn Manselle

The data logged from the period of July 1, 2026 to July 30, 2026. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System. The data should include all selectable columns.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

communications.communication:
Dear Rose Terse: 
Thank you for your interest in public records of Spokane County. Your request has been received and is being processed in accordance with the State of Washington Public Records Act, Chapter 42.56 RCW. Your request was received in this office on 5/12/2026 and given the reference number S028935-051226 for tracking purposes. Spokane County Sheriff provides access to public records in compliance with applicable laws and statutes of the State of Washington. In accordance with the public records law, the Sheriff's office has five business days to respond to a request for public records. Records Requested: To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records: 

A list of non-city-owned devices, such as cameras, automatic license plate readers, and gunshot detection systems, registered and/or integrated with the Sheriff's Office's Fusus Real-Time Crime Center (RTCC) system through the CONNECT SPOKANE COUNTY program (https://connectspokanecounty.org/) sufficient to discern the registration name, full street address, number of internal and external devices, whether devices are registered or integrated, and date/time created. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Rose Terse 

Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2287620/ 
Not all public documents are available in electronic format. If the document(s) requested are not available electronically, we will make them available for inspection or by paper copy in accordance with the Public Records Act, Chapter 42.56 RCW. 
 
Your request will be forwarded to the relevant department(s) to locate the information you seek and to determine the volume and any costs associated with satisfying your request. You will be contacted about the availability and/or provided with copies of the records in question. PLEASE NOTE: The State of Washington Public Records Act, Chapter 42.56 RCW, does not require a governmental body to create new information, to do legal research, or to answer questions. 
 
You can monitor the progress of your request at the link below and you'll receive an email when your request has been completed. 
 
Please be advised that Spokane Regional Emergency Communications ("SREC") is the custodian of 911 and Crime Check audio recordings as well as audio recordings of dispatch and radio traffic. If you are attempting to obtain audio recordings of 911/Crime Check calls and/or radio traffic, you need to submit a separate request to SREC directly. You can submit a records request to SREC via their website, https://www.srec911.com. 
Spokane County

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:
Pursuant to the state Freedom of Information Act, G.L.M. c.66, §10, I hereby request the following records:
I am requesting the compliment and complaint records for uniformed officers within your agency from 2021 to present day.  Please send each complaint as an independent record with the following fields:

Complainant Information
•	Anonymous complaint? — Yes / No
•	Year of birth of complainant
•	Preferred language of complainant Arabic; Brazilian Portuguese; Cape Verdean Creole; Cantonese; Mandarin; English; French; Haitian Creole; Russian; Somali; Spanish; Vietnamese; Other
Demographics
•	Gender identity — Female; Male; Genderqueer/Gender Non-binary; Trans female; Trans male; Prefer not to answer; Not listed
•	Race and ethnicity — Asian; Black/African American; Black; Indigenous; Latino; Middle Eastern/West Asian or North African; American Indian/Alaskan Native; Asian & White; Cape Verdean; Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander; Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander & White; Black/African American & White; Multi-racial; Pacific Islander; White; Other; Decline to answer
•	Sexual orientation/identity — Bisexual; Gay; Lesbian/Same Gender Loving; Questioning/Unsure; Straight/Heterosexual; Decline to answer; Not listed
Incident Information
•	Date of incident
•	Time of incident
•	Citation number
•	Incident neighborhood — Allston; Back Bay; Bay Village; Beacon Hill; Brighton; Charlestown; Chinatown/Leather District; Dorchester; Downtown; East Boston; Fenway/Kenmore; Hyde Park; Jamaica Plain; Mattapan; Mid-Dorchester; Mission Hill; North End; Roslindale; Roxbury; South Boston; South End; West End; West Roxbury; Wharf District

•	Arrested during incident? — Yes / No
•	Injured? — Yes / No
•	Description of injuries
•	Incident description (run through PII redaction)
Officer Involvement:
•	Officer Information
•	Number of officers involved
•	For each officer (up to 5):
•	Name
•	Badge
•	Description
•	More than five officers involved? — additional information
•	Police Vehicle Information
•	Number of police vehicles involved

•	Type

•	Description (run through PII redaction)
•	More than five vehicles involved? — additional information
Witnesses:

Additional Information:
•	Complaint submitted on behalf of someone else? — Yes / No
•	Relationship to complainant
•	Submitted date
Outcome:
•	Status of complaint e.g. investigated, sustained, not sustained

I also request a waiver of all fees for this request, as disclosure of the requested information to me is in the public interest and will contribute to the public’s understanding of operations and activities of the government. This request is being made for research conducted by Spark! at Boston University and will not be used for commercial use.
I expect the request to be filled in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

I also ask you to please redact any information you believe to be exempt and disclose the rest. If you need to discuss this request, I can be reached at 503-807-7815. 

Sincerely,
Spark! Lab
Boston University Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

A report or export from the County's financial system sufficient to show all vendors paid, or issued a purchase order, on behalf of the Chatham County Police Department for the most recently completed fiscal year (July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026) and for the current fiscal year (beginning July 1, 2026) through the date of this request. Please include the vendor name and, if the system maintains one, the vendor number. If the County's standard vendor or accounts-payable report already includes other fields, such as amounts paid, payment dates, purchase order numbers, or the department or cost center, please leave them in. I am not asking the County to create a new compilation.

This is a request for data fields in the County's financial database. Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(f), please provide it in the format in which it is kept or in a standard export format such as a CSV or Excel file.

If these records are held by the County's Finance or Purchasing Department rather than the Police Department, please forward this request to the appropriate department and let me know where it was sent.

Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(1), any labor charge may not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee with the necessary skill and training, and the agency must use the most economical means reasonably calculated to produce the records. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

title: MPSE Workforce and Provider data for Churn Analysis

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: MPSE Workforce and Provider data for Churn Analysis
communications.communication:
Dear Data Practices Compliance Official,

This is a formal request under the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act (MGDPA), Minn. Stat. § 13.03, for public data regarding individual provider enrollment and agency affiliations within the Minnesota Provider Screening and Enrollment (MPSE) system.

1. Request for Remote Inspection

Under Minn. Stat. § 13.03, Subd. 3, I am exercising my right to inspect public data. As inspection is free of charge, I am requesting access to these records in the MPSE in their original digital format.

Reasonable Accommodation: Due to intersecting access barriers related to a qualified disability, I am requesting a reasonable accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Title II.

Strict adherence to a standard physical office environment creates a barrier to my access. Specifically, I require accessible system fonts and a specialized, non-standard ergonomic environment (including custom seating and positioning supports) to review materials at length. As these specific necessary environmental modifications are not feasible to replicate in a standard public government office on a shared terminal, I am requesting access to inspect the public data elements in situ with database tools remotely (via remote desktop, secure VPN, or a read-only digital portal).

This accommodation allows me to utilize my own adaptive workstation to review the material effectively and equitably.

This data is required for a public-interest analysis of provider retention. We are investigating whether a reported 250% turnover rate indicates that case managers are leaving the field before reaching the 24-month cadence of interactive disability-led training sessions with DHS partners, or if they are simply migrating between providers.

Data Requested

I am requesting access to a list of all individual case managers and providers enrolled to provide services at any point between January 2015 and December 2025, including the duration of their enrollment associated with each provider.

To facilitate an efficient remote inspection, please ensure a minimum of the following data points are accessible:

    Individual's Full Name

    Individual's State Provider Number (UMPI)

    Individual's National Provider Number (NPI)

    Agency Name (Employer) (Affiliation Records (MPSE-0603))

    Agency's Provider Number (NPI or UMPI) 

    Enrollment Start Date (per agency) (Enrollment History (MPSE-0604))

    Enrollment End Date (per agency; blank if currently enrolled)

If possible, I would like to be have access to the all public headers, fields and tables in the dataset  Along with the data dictionaries in order to facilitate accurate analysis.

Format and Collaboration

While I am requesting remote inspection to avoid the unnecessary fees and physical barriers, I would prefer to review this in a database. If that is infeasible a SQL dump or export to spreadsheet format (CSV or XLSX) or monthly snapshots similar to the NPI files would be an acceptably alternative allowing me to derive the needed relationships in the data.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

As this work is for a non-commercial, public benefit, I respectfully request a full fee waiver for any copies I may ultimately require after my initial inspection.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

If any of your team members are interested in our findings on churn rate, I would be more than happy to share the finished analysis.

Thank you for your assistance in ensuring this process remains accessible.

Best regards,

Sincerely,

Jonathan Murray | (Please use name/Any Pronouns) 
**Principal, Strategic Systems Innovation Lead, Social Infrastructure & Interdependence** 
* I run on Criptime so it may take a while to respond. Please follow up if I've missed your e-mail, especially if it's urgent.

communications.subject: RE: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: MPSE Workforce and Provider data for Churn Analysis
communications.communication:
Good afternoon, 

Following up on my MNDPA request and the request for payment for data access. 

The request specifically avoids asking DHS create new data, only for it to provide access to the public data in the databases segregated from information protected under the Minnesota Data Practices Act.

I understand the barriers that presents when the data is currently held within databases. I will need to use database tools either remotely or on on a MNDHS or MNIT machine.
The request offered of providing copies as a less burdensome way to comply with the obligations of the MNDPA in lieu of direct inspection.

I am reiterating my request to either have accessible remote access to the data directly or for copies to be provided free of charge. I am familiar with SQL and am happy to work with raw datasets and databases.

It's understandable that the DHS would like to avoid incurring costs. I believe providing access and working with me and others from the disability community to research the patterns the data will show, will greatly benefit the state of Minnesota through savings in case management & HCBS costs.

This isn't without precedent the Department of Health & DHS partnered with Elder Family Voices for related datasets and are providing ongoing technical support and data access for Elder Care IQ. https://eldercareiq.org/home

Elder care IQ is viewed as necessary because as "those vulnerable" we haven't had the agency, autonomy and authority ourselves to prevent abuses from happening to us and to stop them when they do. 

You can start to change that by taking this first step in partnering to create a disability lead and run disability data lab in MN. A place & platform on which  those of us who have already reached our disabled futures can work with Allies, Researchers, journalists, Policymakers and government officials all understand the disabled future we share. 

Until DHS buys into that vision. I would appreciate if you could provide access to the data free of charge as obligations under the MNDPA require.

Open roads and their skies,

Jonathan

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Leominster Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Gang Unit Policies & Database Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

1. Policies and General Orders: All current department policies, general orders, standard operating procedures (SOPs), special orders, training manuals, or memoranda governing the Joliet Police Department's identification, documentation, tracking, and validation of individuals as suspected gang members, associates, or affiliates.
2. Criteria Guidelines: Any documents detailing the explicit threshold criteria used by JPD officers or specialized units (e.g., Gang Unit, Special Operations Group) to determine whether an individual is entered into a gang database or designated as gang-affiliated (including criteria regarding tattoos, clothing, associates, social media, or self-admission).
3. Database Specifications: Records detailing the name, architecture, vendor, and system parameters of any local database, software platform, or intelligence system utilized by JPD to store gang affiliation data.
4. Data Sharing & Interoperability: All agreements, memorandums of understanding (MOUs), or policy documents detailing how JPD shares or receives gang-related data with outside entities (e.g., county sheriff's offices, Illinois State Police, federal agencies, or regional multi-jurisdictional intelligence centers).
5. Auditing, Oversight, and Removal: Any policies, guidelines, or logs concerning the periodic review, auditing, purging, or removal of individuals' names from JPD or shared gang databases, including any provisions allowing individuals to contest or appeal their designation.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

M

My request includes but is not limited to 137, 157, 176, 177, 183, 184, 188, and 214 files. Matthew Petti
